about: The design values of QotaFolio: every value that carries a decision of the look, with its reason. tools/gen writes kit/design/Tokens.swift from design/tokens.json. A token is one value, or a value in each look it varies over: light and dark, plain and with Increase Contrast, or all four, with a form for Reduce Transparency where one exists. A colour is an sRGB hex value, a weight of black, of white or of the look's own ink (black on light, white on dark), or a grey at a weight. A size is in points. A weight is an opacity from 0 to 1. A type role is a size, a weight and whether its digits are monospaced. A motion is a curve and a duration in seconds.

level.why: How much of a limit is left, in three steps, the fuel gauge anyone can read. It is the same three steps on the menu-bar battery, on a card's bar and in the graph, so a glance at any of them is answered the same way. The share left is floor(100 - used), and every surface reaches its step from that one number: deciding from the raw fraction would put a bar one step away from the battery above it. The hues are derived, not picked: one OKLCH hue per band, one lightness per look, and whatever chroma the sRGB gamut offers there, so the resting state is the quietest thing on the panel and the alarm the loudest. They are written out rather than read from the system's colours, because the strip draws into a bitmap whose polarity is an argument, and a card and the battery above it must match to the byte.

plentyAbove.why: Above this share left, half, a level is green. Half a limit in hand is the moment pace starts to matter.

nearlyGoneAtOrBelow.why: At or below this share left, a fifth, a level is red: nearly gone, the same fifth at which a battery goes low.

plenty.why: Green, OKLCH hue 154, a step cooler than the system's 147, at eighty per cent of what the gamut allows: the tone seen nearly all the time, with no news to deliver.

low.why: Amber, hue 78, a gold and not an orange: the Anthropic mark on the same card is a terracotta at hue 40, which an orange bar would be mistaken for. It runs at the gamut's edge because a gold has nowhere else to go.

nearlyGone.why: Red, hue 19, turned from the system's 26 toward crimson for a reader who cannot separate red from green, and pulled back to about ninety per cent of the gamut so it does not drown the other two.

surface.why: The panel's glass and the plates that lie on it. A weight of ink follows the desktop through the glass, where a fixed grey would be a firm line over one wallpaper and invisible over the next.

slabTint.why: The neutral the slab's glass is tinted toward. Set against the glass Apple's own panels are cut from, photographed at the same rect over the same wallpaper: mean saturation 0.46 against Apple's 0.46 in light, 0.39 against 0.38 in dark. The app's only; the Deck has no glass.

standIn.why: A flat stand-in for the panel's glass, for a picture drawn with no window, where glass and materials do not render.

plateFill.why: A card's plate: a flat fill, never a material, which would sample the desktop a second time and show a seam at every edge. White in both looks, because a plate is lighter than the glass it lies on. Under Reduce Transparency the slab goes opaque and a white plate would vanish into it, so the plate turns to the look's own ink and separates by depth.

plateEdgeTop.why: The plate's one-point edge, lit along the top where the material's light comes from. Over a dark desktop it is what holds the plate off the glass.

plateEdgeBottom.why: The same edge seated in a shadow along the bottom. Over a bright desktop the lit half disappears, and the shadow holds the plate off the glass.

plateHoverLift.why: A hovered plate lifts a step: this weight is added to its fill. Nothing moves.

hoverWash.why: The wash of the look's own ink under a hovered control, outside a card: the footer's buttons and a card's actions menu. One number, so every control lifts by the same amount.

track.why: The bar's neutral track, the whole limit unspent: a recess in the plate, in both looks, and Increase Contrast deepens it. White ink on a dark plate would move the track toward the bright fill lying in it. The graph's band over a stretch nobody watched is the same recess.

spent.why: The weight of a spent bar: the full red bar sits back, because there is nothing to do about a limit until it returns. A limit merely nearly gone keeps full weight.

chart.why: The neutrals of a chart: black on a light plate and white on a dark one, at a stated weight, so each follows the plate as it moves with the desktop. Set against the plate as it renders, sampled off the panel: the grid near 1.4 to 1.5 to 1, the rule 2.1 to 2.4, the small print near 6. The graph's own weights are each the least that meets its contrast in every look, on the plate and on the band: 3 to 1 for the ceiling, 4.5 to 1 for every word.

grid.why: The ruled ground: the guide lines and the hours under them. The faintest thing on the plate, there to be measured against, not read.

rule.why: A landmark across the plot: the reset, where the limit ends.

smallPrint.why: The chart's own words, the hour labels and the reset's clock, and the line under the cursor, which is read as closely as they are.

hole.why: The hole through a dot that makes it a ring. A weight leans the way the plate leans: lighter on a light plate, darker on a dark one. A named grey reads as a smudge in the dot, not a hole through it.

words.why: The graph's first words: the forecast's sentence and its strongest labels.

secondaryWords.why: The words that come second: the record's sentence and the caption over the chart. The least weight that meets 4.5 to 1.

ceiling.why: A limit's ceiling, the subject of the picture, so stronger than a rule. The least weight that meets 3 to 1.

range.why: The weight of the instrument's band, how far the limit could reach, in the verdict's colour.

menuBar.why: The strip: one Apple battery per account in the menu bar. Its polarity is the bar's own effective appearance, which follows the wallpaper, so light and dark here mean the bar, not the Mac's setting.

ink.why: Apple's label colour for the bar: white on a dark bar, black on a light one, and full strength with Increase Contrast.

dim.why: The weight an account that is not answering is outlined at, so the eye tells no reading from empty without any other mark.

gap.why: Ink edge to ink edge between two batteries. Six points was chosen over four and five by looking at all three on a real menu bar.

fillInset.why: How far the fill sits inside the battery's wall.

smallestFill.why: A length floor: a bar the eye cannot see is not a reading, and a battery still holding one per cent is not the same picture as one holding none.

panel.why: The panel's fixed numbers. The cards sit inside the slab by its padding, so a card's corner is the slab's corner less the padding, the concentric rule; that stays a formula in code.

maxHeight.why: The tallest the slab grows before its cards scroll.

padding.why: How far the cards sit inside the slab.

anchorGap.why: The space between the menu bar item and the slab's top.

shadowRoomTop.why: The room the window keeps above the slab for the glass's own shadow, measured on macOS 26.4: a Gaussian of sigma 16 points, eight down. Two sigma out the shadow has fallen to one part in 255, so the window can end there and no edge is seen. The app's only; the Deck has no glass.

shadowRoomSide.why: The same shadow's room either side of the slab.

shadowRoomBottom.why: The same shadow's room below the slab.

cardPadding.why: How far a card's content sits inside its plate.

barHeight.why: The bar's height. The strip's fill box is 15 by 6, and the row's bar is the same shape at panel size, chosen against 5 and 8.

nameColumn.why: The limit's name column. Session, Weekly and a model's name all fit; fixing it lines the percentages up down every card.

percentColumn.why: The percentage column, right-aligned so 8% sits under 38% and 100%.

markSize.why: A provider's mark, and the advisory's icon in its place.

hitTarget.why: Every control on the panel is reachable inside at least this square.

glyphWell.why: A control's glyph sits in this square inside its hit target.

headerHeight.why: The card header's height, so the actions menu beside it lands on its centre whether or not the account has a plan line.

typography.why: Always the system font, with no tracking of its own, so the font's own optical size and tracking apply. Four sizes, 10 to 13 points, for words, and three for symbols. Every number that changes has digits of one width, so it does not shift as it counts.

label.why: A limit's name on its row, and the plan in the instrument.

body.why: The body: the word used, a card's state, an advisory, a sentence.

bodyFigures.why: A sentence that carries numbers: the graph's two sentences, the instrument's spend line.

note.why: A card's header note, such as Back at 21:37.

caption.why: Small print: the plan under an account's name.

captionFigures.why: Small print with numbers: a limit's reset, the time of the newest reading, the cursor's readout.

axis.why: A chart's words: the hours under it and its quiet labels. The graph measures each word in this role to place it, so the measure and the drawing read one value.

axisMedium.why: A chart's label that names a mark: a forecast's end, the reset's clock.

axisStrong.why: A chart's strongest label: the forecast that matters most, and now.

glyph.why: A control's symbol: the footer's buttons and a card's actions menu.

advisoryGlyph.why: The symbol of an advisory row, in the mark's place.

aboutGlyph.why: The symbol on the About tab.

motion.why: The panel's motions. Someone who has asked for less movement gets a form of the change with no travel in it, not the same travel made quicker.

card.why: A card opening and closing: the whole slab travels about 110 points. A spring with no bounce never snaps, so the length need not supply the gentleness; it arrives at nine tenths of the distance in 0.19 s and eases the rest.

dissolve.why: How a change arrives when nothing may travel: the panel takes its new height in one frame and the content dissolves into it.

hover.why: A hovered plate or control lifts or washes in.
